Rae: Heads-up: Conductivity-13B int4 warm onboarding showing puzzling OOMs under bursty small-requests pattern. Single-turn NLP tasks are fine; multi-turn chat tests hit OOMs and slight coherence hits.
Diego: what's the test profile? ctx sizes, gen lengths, batching?
Rae: convo-sim suite: mixed ctx 512-4096, avg gen=320. Defaults used: max_new_tokens=512, prefetch_limit=3072, batch_window_ms=18, batch_cap=10. OOM rate ~0.07% in 30k-run.
Priya: sounds like fragmentation from aggressive prefetch + long gen. Any logs?
Rae: pasted snippet from affected worker: 
```
[2024-10-15T07:42:11Z] gen:start model=conductivity-13b-int4 req=0x7a ctx_len=3840 gen=480
[2024-10-15T07:42:11Z] prefetch: queued 24 chunks avg=44KB
[2024-10-15T07:42:11Z] alloc: requested_contig=1.12GB free_contig=680MB total_free=5.1GB
[2024-10-15T07:42:11Z] compactor: run skipped (low priority)
[2024-10-15T07:42:11Z] OOM: failed to assemble contiguous block after evict
```
Diego: compactor skipped suggests it's not proactive enough. Two quick knobs: reduce prefetch_limit to 1024 for convo endpoints, lower default max_new_tokens to 256, enable compactor with low CPU budget. Also try kv.reserve_gap to keep a reserved contiguous area.
Priya: kv.reserve_gap? haven't used that widely. Explain please.
Diego: allocator hint: reserve_gap=N keeps N MB contiguous reserved per worker to avoid split_allocs for large generations. For int4 models with long ctx+gen it's handy: reserve_gap=512 means we try to keep a 512MB contiguous slab. Cost: slightly higher idle fragmentation but fewer mid-run OOMs.
Rae: proposed quick experiments 
- max_new_tokens=256
- prefetch_limit=1024
- compactor.enable=true, compactor.rate=0.18, compaction_threshold=0.6
- allocator.reserve_gap_mb=512 (per-worker)
- kv.evict_min_prefix=2048 (evict only very long prefixes)
Priya: also add an A/B: deferred-dequant=true as a runtime option (defer dequant of KV until generation start) to reduce interim scratch usage. Might trade small latency.
Rae: running rbench with the config: 
```
rbench --model conductivity-13b-int4 --suite convo-sim-long --concurrency 20 --batch-cap 8 --max_new_tokens 256 --prefetch_limit 1024 --allocator.reserve_gap_mb 512 --compactor.rate 0.18
```
Bench-bot: perf run queued -> https://ci.internal/runs/83421 (artifacts + token breakdown)
Rae: first 10k requests: OOMs=0, coherence delta -0.8% (was -2.7%), p95 latency +4% vs prior int4 but p95 still ~20% below fp16. CPU of compactor on workers rose ~6%.
Diego: good. How about deferred-dequant trial? That might shave the coherence hit further if dequant noise is causing state differences.
Priya: I'll enable deferred-dequant on a small canary (5%) with same knobs, monitor hallucination and multi-turn consistency. Add rollback triggers: OOMs > 0.03% OR coherence drop > 1.5% OR p95 regress > 25%.
Rae: canary plan: 5% traffic for 48h, dashboards: OOM rate, convo-consistency score, p95/p99, compactor CPU, and token cost. I'll post link when deployed.
SRE-team: FYI - please watch for host-level swap activity and tenant memory pressure during ramp. We'll alert if host OOM risk rises.
Bench-bot: Canary deployed -> canary-id=conductivity-canary-2024-10-15 targets=5%
Rae: update after 16h: deferred-dequant canary shows OOMs=0, coherence delta -0.5%, p95 +6%, compactor CPU +7%, cost/token -2.9x vs fp16. Looks safe to step to 25%.
Diego: excellent. Follow-up: add "int4-conductivity-recipe" to onboarding templates recommending reserve_gap_mb=512, prefetch_limit<=1024, default max_new_tokens=256 for convo endpoints, and flag deferred-dequant as experimental knob.
Priya: I'll open PR for model-configs + short rationale doc with perf links. Rae: please attach final perf artifacts to the PR.
Rae: will do. Thanks all for the fast triage. :thumbsup:
